title: Gribbly's Day Out
build: Hewson's cassette release: a raw TAP of the original tape, one turbo-loaded block

credits.role: Design and programming, as the title screen credits it

tools.host: Linux x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04.5, no display (cloud container)
tools.simulator: kit/c64/cpu6502.js, for the tests of the sound driver's and level_result's ports (test_sound.js, test_level.js)
tools.browser: Chromium 141.0.7390.37 (Playwright 1.56.1's), headless, for the page checks
tools.subagents: one checker agent on the Agent tool's general-purpose type for 60-verify's sample of 80 comments; all other work by one agent

exclude: runtime: the title and status-panel text screen and its sprite pointers, printed and set by the code
unused: a gap in the loaded file between empty_hook and the sound driver, a RAM fill pattern of $00 and $FF with a few stray bytes; nothing runs or reads it
runtime: the level map, 256 columns by 64 rows, built at every level start over the load's copies of the level data and scene lists, which start_game has moved to $E000 and $C200
runtime: the soil row under the map and the wall's copy after it, built by make_soil_row

regions: zero page: sprite parameters, pointers, score, Gribbly's movement, psi, sound driver state
pause copy of the clock, levels done, best score, the Gribblet and creature tables
messages, the volume string and the panel's labels
the collision table and scatter_rocks' template record
number words and the end-of-level messages
column shapes and templates for the ground and the floating scenery
stray code from another program, never run
the text font, upper and lower halves
the play tiles: web, controls, ground, Gribblets, scenery, water
sprite shapes $C0-$FF: Gribbly, bubbles, creatures and the materialising pieces
the hidden memory editor and the text printer
start-up, title pages, the play loop, creatures, Gribbly, the web, the raster chain
clock, title pages, status words, bars and messages
animation groups, web triangles, level colours, movement constants, Gribbly's face, the best-score line
per-level pointers: scene lists, web layouts, start columns, names
scene lists of levels 12, 6, 8, 13, 15, 3, 1 and 2, and more shapes
instruments, sound effects, note frequencies and the title tune
